settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Configure NoteFast options. Local-first; database backups, Markdown archive and AI are all optional.

maintenance.autoHint: Run maintenance only physically deletes residue older than 30 days (plus stale history and vector generations); newer residue stays. A pass also runs every 6 hours. Vacuum reclaims deleted pages and truncates the WAL.
maintenance.vacuumMessage: VACUUM physically reclaims space from deleted data and may shrink the database file. On large databases it can stall briefly for a few seconds; keep the app open during the run.

about.blurb: NoteFast is an AI-native Markdown knowledge base that automatically indexes, links, and searches every note.
about.checkFailed: Check failed. Try again later or open
about.manualHint: Update checks only run when you click; the app does not phone home on launch.

localData.title: Local data
localData.helpTip: SQLite, images, and the Markdown shadow copy live in this directory. The shadow is one-way: editing those .md files does not write back.
localData.pathHintNative: In the desktop app this path is on this computer. Use the button below to reveal it in the file manager.
localData.pathHintServer: This is a path on the server, not on this computer.
localData.shadowHint: Notes are written to Markdown as they change, grouped by first tag. One-way copy: editing these .md files does not write back; SQLite remains the source of truth. Images point at the existing media/ store and are not duplicated.
localData.loadFailed: Could not read the data directory
localData.revealFailed: Could not open the file manager
localData.modeDbHint: Notes live in the data directory below. To make them plain files any tool can open, see Vault mode.
localData.modeVaultHint: The .md files in this folder are authoritative; the data directory below only holds the index and can be rebuilt from scratch.

imageUpload.description: Images are always stored locally first. Configure the hosting command independently of auto-upload: with auto-upload off you can still upload from the library or an image. With it on, pasting also uploads asynchronously; failures stay local.
imageUpload.modeOffHint: Paste and import stay local; upload from the library or an image when you want
imageUpload.modeAutoHint: Also uploads asynchronously on paste; failures stay local
imageUpload.commandHint: Executable name (on PATH) or absolute path; the image path is appended as the last argument
imageUpload.contractHint: Images stay stored locally and render reliably inside the app; after a successful upload, the hosted URL is used only when exporting or sharing a document.
imageUpload.testDraftNote: This test uses the current configuration in the form above (including unsaved changes)

termDict.title: Entity Dictionary
termDict.helpTip: Declared alias → canonical-name rules: extraction, retrieval and merging all converge on the canonical name; industry term packs can be imported wholesale
termDict.description: Declare canonical-name ↔ alias rules (e.g. wafer ↔ 晶圆). Saving an entry applies immediately: the Entities page, global search, and MCP find the entity by either name; note search expands aliases to the canonical name. An empty dictionary changes nothing.
termDict.saved: Saved and applied — search by canonical name or alias
termDict.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this entity? (optional; takes priority over AI-generated)
termDict.importHint: Paste an industry dictionary JSON or pick a file; entries merge by canonical name

vault.title: Vault mode
vault.helpTip: The folder is authoritative and SQLite is a rebuildable index: this page shows index state, reconcile results and write-back conflicts
vault.watcherInactive: File watching is off (changes need a manual rebuild)
vault.conflictHint: On conflict the on-disk version is kept as-is and the NoteFast version is saved as a sibling .notefast-conflict-<time>.md copy, which is then ingested as a new document.
vault.syncTargetNone: No storage connection or local directory selected
vault.syncLocalDirDesc: LocalFS target (debug / several instances on one machine); takes precedence over the storage connection
vault.syncPrefixDesc: Remote object key prefix; empty means the root
vault.syncIntervalDesc: 0 = manual only, or push only when files change
vault.syncPushSummary: Scanned {{scanned}} · changed {{changed}} · uploaded {{uploaded}} objects · deleted {{tombstones}} · mtime-only {{touched}}
vault.syncNoConflicts: No conflicts in the last pull
vault.syncHint: File sync moves files only, not the index: the watcher ingests them once they land on disk. Running iCloud / Dropbox / Syncthing on the same folder makes them delete each other's files — keep exactly one.
vault.syncForeignHints: Third-party sync traces detected ({{tools}}): two sync tools on one folder delete each other's files — keep exactly one.
vault.disabledHint: Notes live in SQLite, not as .md files in a folder. In vault mode your Markdown folder becomes authoritative and SQLite is only a rebuildable index.
vault.disabledHowTo: How to switch to vault mode
vault.disabledDesktop: Desktop: menu Vault → Open folder as vault… (Windows: use the button on the start screen)
vault.disabledDocker: Docker: mount your notes folder at /vault and set VAULT_PATH=/vault (on Docker Desktop also set VAULT_USE_POLLING=true)
vault.disabledServer: Self-hosted: start with VAULT_PATH=~/Notes (see the vault mode section in the README)
vault.disabledMigration: To move existing notes, see docs/vault-migration.md. There is no in-place conversion; the old instance is left untouched.
vault.pollingAuto: Native file events do not reach this folder, so polling was enabled automatically (set VAULT_USE_POLLING to override).
vault.pickVaultHint: Restarts NoteFast with the folder you pick: its Markdown becomes the source of truth. Your database-mode data stays on disk and you can switch back at any time.
vault.leaveVaultHint: Restarts NoteFast in database mode. The files in your folder are untouched and the index stays on disk.
